Jasionowka New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Słomianka, Poland

Not demolished. Jews are first recorded in Jasionówka in the 16th century, developing significantly through the following century under a kehilla subordinate to Tykocin's Jewish community; population reached 1,306 (74%) by 1921. Germans murdered nearly all the town's Jews at Treblinka in early 1943. This cemetery, established in the early 19th century, remained in use until WWII, when it also received Holocaust victims, including 8 people found hiding and shot in nearby Kamionka village. At least 150 tombstones survive in varying condition, the oldest (1831) commemorating Cwi, son of Mosze. Property rights transfer to the Jewish community remains pending as of this record.
